s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Rebellion
s.d: (derivative of {L:στάσις<SDBG:στάσις:000000>}[a] ‘insurrection,’ {D:39.34}) a person who engages in insurrection

s.dp: Reconciliation, Forgiveness › Reconciliation
s.d: to reestablish proper friendly interpersonal relations after these have been disrupted or broken (the componential features of this series of meanings involve (1) disruption of friendly relations because of (2) presumed or real provocation (3) overt behavior designed to remove hostility, and (4) restoration of original friendly relations){N:001}
s.g: to reconcile; to make things right with one another; reconciliation
s.c: Because of the variety and complexity of the components involved in reconciliation, it is often necessary to use an entire phrase in order to communicate satisfactorily the meanings of the terms in this subdomain. In some languages, however, reconciliation is often spoken of in idiomatic terms, for example, ‘to cause to become friends again,’ ‘to cause to snap fingers again’ (a symbol of friendly interpersonal relations in many parts of Africa), ‘to cause to be one again,’ or ‘to take away the separation.’ A particularly crucial element in terms for reconciliation is the assigning of responsibility for original guilt in causing the estrangement. Some terms, for example, imply that the individual who initiates reconciliation is by doing so admitting his guilt in causing the estrangement. This, of course, provides a completely untenable meaning for reconciliation in speaking of God reconciling people to himself through Christ.|In a number of languages the contextual basis for an expression for reconciliation is often found in terms relating to the reconciliation of husbands and wives. Such expressions fit in well with many contexts in the Scriptures, especially in speaking of reconciliation of people to God, since God is frequently referred to as the husband and the believers as the wife.|This is the only instance of συναλλάσσω in the NT, and it has εἰς εἰρήνην added to emphasize peace as the goal, although the feature of making peace between previously hostile individuals is already implicit in the act of reconciliation.

s.dp: Communication › Witness, Testify
s.d: to join one’s witness to that of others
s.g: to add one’s witness to; to witness together with

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Attack
s.d: to join in attacking
s.c: In ⟦Acts 24:9|Acts 24:9⟧ συνεπιτίθεμαι does not involve physical force but strong verbal opposition. It may therefore be more appropriate to translate ‘they opposed him strongly with their words’ or ‘they spoke very strongly against him.’

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: to work out a joint arrangement
s.g: to agree on; to arrange together; joint agreement; joint arrangement; mutual agreement

s.dp: Linear Movement › Follow, Accompany
s.d: to accompany someone, with explicit marking of association

s.dp: Perform, Do › Do, Perform
s.d: to engage in an activity together with someone else
s.g: to work together with; to be active together with

s.dp: Perform, Do › Work, Toil
s.d: one who works together with someone else

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: the movement of two or more objects to the same location{N:001}
s.g: to gather together; to come together; to go together; to meet; to assemble
s.c: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in terms referring to gathering or assembling of animate beings. The distinctions are usually based upon the number of individuals, the distance which they have come, and whether or not the individuals in question constitute a membership group or whether they are merely a loose aggregation. In view of these types of distinctions, it is likely that quite different terms will be required for the various contexts listed for this set of related meanings.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go With, Travel With
s.d: to come/go together with one or more other persons
s.g: to come with; to go with; to accompany

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sexual Relations
s.d: a figurative extension of meaning of {L:συνέρχομαι<SDBG:συνέρχομαι:000000>}[a] ‘to come together,’ {D:15.123}
s.c: In almost all languages there are euphemistic ways of speaking about sexual intercourse, and the use of γινώσκω and συνέρχομαι is illustrative of this in the Greek NT. It is possible to translate γινώσκω in ⟦Luke 1:34|Luke 1:34⟧ as simply ‘for I am not married to a man,’ and likewise, συνέρχομαι in ⟦Matthew 1:18|Matthew 1:18⟧ may be rendered as ‘before they were married.’ In some languages one may use such expressions as ‘before they were joined’ or ‘before they slept together’ or ‘before they discovered one another.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: to eat together with others
s.c: In a number of languages a term meaning ‘to eat together with others’ is completely distinct from an expression referring to eating by one person. Furthermore, a term meaning basically ‘to eat together’ may focus primarily on conviviality and feasting rather than merely on the process of eating. In ⟦Acts 11:3|Acts 11:3⟧ there is no indication of ‘feasting.’

s.dp: Understand
s.d: (derivative of {L:συνίημι<SDBG:συνίημι:000000>}[a] ‘to understand,’ {D:32.5}) that which is understood or comprehended

s.dp: Understand › Capacity for Understanding
s.d: to be able to understand and evaluate
s.g: to be able to comprehend; to understand; to be intelligent; insight; intelligence

s.dp: Understand › Capacity for Understanding
s.d: pertaining to being able to understand and evaluate

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Agree, Consent
s.d: to decide with someone else that something is preferable or good
s.g: to agree to; to consent to

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: to join with others in eating elaborate meals or banquets
s.c: ‘To feast together’ may be expressed in some languages merely as ‘to eat a great deal together with others’ or ‘to join with others in filling one’s stomach’ or ‘to eat with others more than one should.’

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Attack
s.d: to join in attacking

s.dp: Control, Rule › Control, Restrain
s.d: to exercise continuous control over someone or something
s.c: There is usually no difficulty in speaking of ‘control’ if it is performed by a person as in ⟦1 Peter 2:13|1 Peter 2:13⟧. However, it may not be possible to speak of ‘death’ having control, unless the language in question can personify death. In some instances ⟦Acts 2:24|Acts 2:24⟧ (see LN 37.16) must be rendered as ‘it was impossible for him to continue to be dead,’ and in ⟦2 Corinthians 5:14|2 Corinthians 5:14⟧ ‘Christ’s love controls us’ may be rendered as ‘the fact that Christ loves us causes us to act as we do.’

s.dp: Control, Rule › Guard, Watch Over
s.d: to continue to hold in custody
s.g: to guard; to keep watch; custody
s.c: The act of holding someone in custody or guarding an individual may be expressed as ‘standing guard to see that someone will not escape’ or ‘watching carefully so that one cannot run off’ or ‘tying someone up so that he cannot leave.’

s.dp: Physical Impact › Press
s.d: to press in hard from all sides
s.g: to press in; to crowd around

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Hear
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to hold the ears closed) to refuse to listen to what is being said
s.g: to refuse to listen; to refuse to pay attention
s.c: In some languages the refusal to hear may be expressed idiomatically as ‘they put their hands over their ears’ or ‘they closed their ears’ or ‘the words never entered their heads.’

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: to experience a state or condition, generally involving duration

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: to experience great psychological pressure and anxiety
s.g: to be distressed; to be troubled

s.dp: Aspect › Continue
s.d: to continue with close attention and devotion
s.g: to continue to give oneself to; to continue to apply oneself to

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to be held together from) to be in a mental state between two alternatives
s.g: to be pulled in two directions; to be betwixt and between; to have conflicting thoughts
s.c: In a number of languages the rendering of this statement in ⟦Philippians 1:23|Philippians 1:23⟧ must be expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘my mind is pulling me in two directions’ or ‘my thoughts are going in two different directions’ or ‘my heart is speaking two different words to me.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Happy, Glad, Joyful
s.d: to be happy as the result of the pleasure derived from some experience or state
s.g: to rejoice in; to delight in
s.c: In a number of languages one may speak of ‘one’s inner being’ as ‘one’s liver’ or ‘one’s heart’ or ‘one’s abdomen’ (employing a reference to one of the organs of the body as a focal element of the personality). But in some languages a more figurative and idiomatic expression may be employed, for example, ‘one’s inner counterpart’ or ‘the little one who stands inside of a person.’ It is often this central or crucial aspect of the personality which must be referred to in contexts speaking of the type of pleasure or delight which one might have in the law of God.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Custom, Tradition
s.d: a pattern of behavior more or less fixed by tradition and generally sanctioned by the society
s.c: In a number of languages there is no noun for ‘custom’ or ‘habit,’ but the same meaning is communicated by verbal aspects or adverbial phrases indicating habitual action. For example, in the case of ⟦John 19:40|John 19:40⟧ one may translate in some languages ‘as is the way in which Jews always bury people,’ and for ⟦1 Corinthians 11:16|1 Corinthians 11:16⟧ one may translate ‘this is not what we constantly do.’

s.dp: Time › Indefinite Units of Time: Age, Lifetime, Interval, Period
s.d: a person who is of one’s own age

s.dp: Funerals and Burial
s.d: to bury someone along with someone else
s.c: In ⟦Romans 6:4|Romans 6:4⟧ συνθάπτω is used figuratively, since it evidently had not yet acquired a conventional figurative meaning. In a number of languages it is necessary to mark this figurative usage by means of a simile, for example, ‘we were, so to speak, buried with him.’

s.dp: Physical Impact › Break, Break Through
s.d: to break or shatter a solid object into pieces, with the implication of destruction
s.g: to break into pieces; to shatter

s.dp: Physical Impact › Press
s.d: to press in hard from all sides
s.g: to press in; to crowd around

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Sorrow, Regret
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to break the heart) to cause great sorrow and grief
s.g: to make grieve; to break one’s heart
s.c: It is rare that one can reproduce in a literal form the idiom συνθρύπτω τὴν καρδίαν. A frequent equivalent of ‘to break one’s heart’ is ‘to cause one to cry.’ In some languages one may even have ‘to cause one’s heart to cry.’

s.dp: Understand
s.d: to employ one’s capacity for understanding and thus to arrive at insight
s.g: to understand; to comprehend; to perceive; to have insight into

s.dp: Understand › Capacity for Understanding
s.d: to be able to understand and evaluate
s.g: to be able to comprehend; to understand; to be intelligent; insight; intelligence

s.dp: Communication › Recommend, Propose
s.d: to indicate approval of a person or event, with the implication that others adopt the same attitude

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to cause something to be known by action
s.g: to make known by action; to demonstrate; to show
s.c: In a number of languages the expression ‘to show oneself to be’ may best be rendered as ‘to cause people to know that one is,’ and therefore this expression in ⟦2 Corinthians 6:4|2 Corinthians 6:4⟧ may be rendered as ‘in everything causing people to know by what we do that we are servants of God.’

s.dp: Whole, Unite, Part, Divide › Unite
s.d: to bring together or hold together something in its proper or appropriate place or relationship
s.c: In ⟦Colossians 1:17|Colossians 1:17⟧ it may not be easy to indicate clearly the relationship of the phrase ‘in him’ to the rest of the expression, namely, ‘all things hold together.’ Some translations have expanded the expression ‘in him’ to ‘in union with him’ or ‘in view of the fact that we are joined together with him.’|It is also possible to understand ἐν αὐτῷ as indicating agent, so that this expression in ⟦Colossians 1:17|Colossians 1:17⟧ may mean ‘by means of him all things hold together.’

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Stand
s.d: to stand together with someone
s.c: It is, of course, essential to avoid the idiomatic meaning of ‘to stand with’ in a sense of ‘to support.’ In this context the emphasis is simply upon being present with.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Exist
s.d: to come into existence, with the implication of acquiring form and substance
s.g: to come into existence; to be formed

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go With, Travel With
s.d: to travel together with
s.c: In a number of languages it may be necessary in speaking of ‘travelling’ to indicate whether a single journey is involved or whether one is going from place to place. In ⟦Acts 9:7|Acts 9:7⟧ it is evidently a single journey.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come/Go With, Travel With
s.d: (derivative of {L:συνοδεύω<SDBG:συνοδεύω:000000>} ‘to travel with,’ {D:15.149}) a group of persons travelling together
s.g: a group of travellers; a group of those travelling with

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: to conduct oneself in relation to a person with whom one lives
s.g: to live with; to conduct oneself with

s.dp: Building, Constructing
s.d: to be built together with some other object or objects
s.c: The context of ⟦Ephesians 2:22|Ephesians 2:22⟧ is, of course, figurative.

s.dp: Communication › Converse, Discuss
s.d: to converse with someone, including a clear implication as to reciprocal response
s.g: to talk with; to speak with; to converse

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be at a place which is next to something else
s.g: to be next to; to border on
s.c: In a number of languages the concept of ‘being next to’ may be best expressed as ‘there was no space between.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: a state of mental distress, involving acute anxiety

s.dp: Communication › Command, Order
s.d: to give detailed instructions as to what must be done{N:001}
s.g: to order; to instruct; to tell; to command

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Duration of Time: Beginning, End
s.d: a point of time marking the end of a duration
s.c: As in the case of a number of expressions involving ‘end,’ it may be important to use a verb meaning ‘to finish,’ for example, ‘so it will be like that when the age finishes’ or ‘… when there isn’t any more of the age.’

s.dp: Aspect › Complete, Finish, Succeed
s.d: to bring an activity to a successful finish{N:001}
s.g: to complete; to finish; to end; to accomplish
s.c: It is also possible to render this phrase in ⟦Romans 9:28|Romans 9:28⟧ as ‘for he will settle the account,’ the implication being that he will accomplish what he has said he would do.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Exist
s.d: to cause to exist by virtue of its having been finally accomplished
s.g: to cause to exist; to accomplish

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Duration of Time: Beginning, End
s.d: (derivative of {L:συντέλεια<SDBG:συντέλεια:000000>} ‘end,’ {D:67.66}) to occur or happen at the end of a duration
s.g: to end; to come to an end

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Duration of Time: Beginning, End
s.d: to cause a duration to come to an abrupt end, with the implication of sooner than expected
s.g: to cut short; to shorten; to bring to an end
s.c: There are a number of different opinions with regard to the meaning of συντέμνω in ⟦Romans 9:28|Romans 9:28⟧. Translators are accordingly encouraged to consult commentaries and to provide for significantly different interpretations in translations.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to cause something to continue along with something else
s.g: to keep together; to preserve both

s.dp: Memory and Recall › Storing of Information
s.d: to exert mental effort in storing information so as to have continual access and use of it
s.g: to cause oneself to be fully aware of; to keep in mind; to remember
s.c: An equivalent of ‘to keep in mind’ may be ‘to keep thinking about’ or ‘to continue to think about’ or even ‘not to stop thinking about.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to a relatively brief period of time, implying some measure of reduction or shortening

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to come together quickly to form a crowd
s.g: to rush together; to run together; to assemble quickly

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of συντρέχω ‘to run with,’ not occurring in the NT) to be closely associated with others in a particular type of behavior or conduct
s.g: to join in living; to be closely associated with

s.dp: Physical Impact › Break, Break Through
s.d: to break or shatter a solid object into pieces, with the implication of destruction
s.g: to break into pieces; to shatter

s.dp: Physical Impact › Press
s.d: to cause damage to an object by crushing
s.c: It is difficult to know precisely what the reference is in the use of συντρίβω in ⟦Luke 9:39|Luke 9:39⟧. The obvious result is severe pain, but it is not possible to tell precisely what symptoms are involved in what is described as being crushed by the demon.

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Conquer
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:συντρίβω<SDBG:συντρίβω:000001>}[b] ‘to crush,’ {D:19.46}) to overcome, with the resulting crushing of the power of the opposition

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Destroy
s.d: a state of destruction and ruin
s.c: In some languages it is impossible to speak of ‘leaving ruin’ except in the sense of going off from ruin. Accordingly, it may be necessary to render this expression in ⟦Romans 3:16|Romans 3:16⟧ as ‘they cause ruin and misery wherever they go.’

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations of the Same Generation
s.d: a person offered parental care and/or adoption along with the reference person, though not related by blood
s.c: It is possible, however, that σύντροφος in ⟦Acts 13:1|Acts 13:1⟧ has the meaning of ‘a close friend from childhood’ (see LN 34.15).|In some languages ‘a foster brother’ may be referred to as ‘a person who becomes a brother by being adopted’ or ‘a person who grows up just as though he were a brother.’

s.dp: Association › Associate
s.d: a close friend on the basis of having been brought up together
s.g: close friend; intimate friend; friend since childhood
s.c: Some scholars, however, understand σύντροφος in ⟦Acts 13:1|Acts 13:1⟧ as being an instance of σύντροφος 'foster brother' (see LN 10.51).

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come Near, Approach
s.d: to come near to or to reach, with the implication of some type of association
s.g: to reach; to get near to

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian woman in the church of Philippi

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Hypocrisy, Pretense
s.d: to act hypocritically along with others
s.g: to pretend together; to join in hypocrisy

s.dp: Help, Care For › Help
s.d: to help by joining in an activity or effort
s.c: In a number of instances it is not necessary to specify the joint effort or activity, since this is supplied by the context itself as, for example, in ⟦Luke 5:7|Luke 5:7⟧ in which ‘coming to help’ indicates clearly the joint efforts. But in some languages it may be important to use a specific expression rather than a generic one. Accordingly, ‘to come and help them’ in ⟦Luke 5:7|Luke 5:7⟧ may be rendered as ‘to come and work with them.’

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Pain, Suffering
s.d: to suffer great anguish or pain together, with the implication of an important and creative event

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: a plan for taking secret action against someone or some institution, with the implication of an oath binding the conspirators

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city on the east coast of Sicily

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a region to the north and east of Palestine and known as Aram in OT times

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Συρία<SDBG:Συρία:000000>} ‘Syria,’ {D:93.589}) a person who is a native of Syria

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of Συροφοινικία ‘Syro-Phoenicia,’ not occurring in the NT) a woman who is a native of Syro-Phoenicia
s.c: See also discussion at LN 10.1.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: two shallow and treacherous Mediterranean gulfs along the north African coastline

s.dp: Linear Movement › Pull, Draw, Drag
s.d: to pull or drag, requiring force because of the inertia of the object being dragged
s.g: to pull; to drag; to draw

s.dp: Linear Movement › Lead, Bring, Take
s.d: to drag or pull by physical force, often implying resistance
s.g: to drag; to lead by force

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: to cause a person to shake violently in convulsions
s.g: to throw into convulsions; to throw into a fit

s.dp: Communication › Non-Verbal Communication
s.d: a sign which has been previously agreed upon as having a particular meaning or significance
s.c: If a language has no specific term for ‘signal’ or ‘sign,’ one may indicate the implications of σύσσημον by translating the first part of ⟦Mark 14:44|Mark 14:44⟧ as follows: ‘the one who betrayed him told them how he would indicate who Jesus was; he said, The one whom I kiss is the man.’

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › General
s.d: a person who is a member of a group, with emphasis upon his coordinate relation to other members of the group
s.c: The concept of ‘being a co-member’ may be expressed in some languages as ‘a person who is counted along with others,’ so that in ⟦Ephesians 3:6|Ephesians 3:6⟧ one may translate ‘the Gentiles are counted along with the Jews in sharing in the promise’ or even ‘the Gentiles along with the Jews share in the promise.’

s.dp: Communication › Recommend, Propose
s.d: (derivative of {L:συνίστημι<SDBG:συνίστημι:000000>}[a] ‘to recommend,’ {D:33.344}) pertaining to being commended or recommended
s.c: It may be necessary to restructure considerably the components in an expression such as ‘we need letters of recommendation to you,’ for example, ‘we need letters written to you which recommend us’ or ‘… which say, These men are good.’

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: to crucify someone at the same time that another person is being crucified

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: to extend in time, with focus upon the end point
s.g: to draw near; to draw to a close

s.dp: Linear Movement › Carry, Bear
s.d: to remove from a place by taking away or carrying away
s.c: In ⟦Acts 5:6|Acts 5:6⟧ συστέλλω may also be interpreted as meaning ‘to wrap up’ (see LN 79.119).

s.dp: Features of Objects › Wrapped
s.d: to wrap up an object, with the implication of getting it ready to remove
s.g: to wrap up; to make a bundle of
s.c: For another interpretation of συστέλλω in ⟦Acts 5:6|Acts 5:6⟧, see LN 15.200.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Laugh, Cry, Groan
s.d: to groan or to sigh together with someone else
s.g: to groan together; to sigh together
s.c: In ⟦Romans 8:22|Romans 8:22⟧ συστενάζω is used figuratively. It may be difficult to speak of ‘all of creation groans together,’ since the phrase ‘all of creation’ would seem to be a total unit. It may therefore be necessary to translate ‘all of creation groans together’ as ‘all parts of the creation groan together’ or ‘everything that has been created is groaning at the same time.’

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Archetype, Corresponding Type [Antitype]
s.d: to correspond to something else in certain significant features
s.g: to correspond to; to stand for; to be a figure of; to represent
s.c: In a number of languages συστοιχέω in a context such as ⟦Galatians 4:25|Galatians 4:25⟧ may be best rendered as ‘points to’ or ‘is really talking about,’ so that one may render this expression in ⟦Galatians 4:25|Galatians 4:25⟧ as ‘Mount Sinai … really points to the present Jerusalem’ or ‘Hagar … really points to the present Jerusalem.’ The full form of ⟦Galatians 4:25|Galatians 4:25⟧ may be rendered as ‘Hagar, who stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia, represents the present Jerusalem.’

s.dp: Association › Associate
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of συστρατιώτης ‘fellow soldier,’ not occurring in the NT) one who serves in arduous tasks or undergoes severe experiences together with someone else
s.g: one who struggles along with; one who works arduously along with; fellow struggler
s.c: A strictly literal translation of συστρατιώτης in ⟦Philemon 1:2|Philemon 1:2⟧ might imply that Paul himself was a soldier and therefore, in a sense, a secret agent of some military force. Accordingly, it may be necessary to employ a simile, for example, ‘who works like a fellow soldier’ or ‘one who experiences great hardships along with us.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to cause to come together, whether of animate or inanimate objects
s.g: to gather together; to call together

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: the movement of two or more objects to the same location{N:001}
s.g: to gather together; to come together; to go together; to meet; to assemble
s.c: In a number of languages important distinctions are made in terms referring to gathering or assembling of animate beings. The distinctions are usually based upon the number of individuals, the distance which they have come, and whether or not the individuals in question constitute a membership group or whether they are merely a loose aggregation. In view of these types of distinctions, it is likely that quite different terms will be required for the various contexts listed for this set of related meanings.

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Riot
s.d: disorderly mob revolt, with special implications of uproar and disturbance
s.c: In a number of languages the meaning of ‘riot’ may be best expressed as ‘people shouting strongly against’ or ‘people shouting and fighting against’ or ‘a mob shouting against the government.’

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: a plan devised by a number of persons who agree to act against someone or some institution
s.c: See συνωμοσία LN 30.73 and its footnote.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Particular Patterns of Behavior
s.d: to form or mold one’s behavior in accordance with a particular pattern or set of standards
s.g: to shape one’s behavior; to conform one’s life
s.c: In order to express the concept of ‘conforming one’s life’ it may be necessary in some languages to indicate the factor of change, for example, ‘to change one’s life so that it will be like.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city in Samaria

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the son of Hamor (τοῦ Συχέμ, apparatus)

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city in Samaria

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: slaughtering, either of animals or persons; in contexts referring to persons, the implication is of violence and mercilessness{N:001}

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judge, Condemn, Acquit
s.d: (an idiom, literally: day of slaughter) a time of destructive judgment
s.c: The reference of the phrase ἡμέρᾳ σφαγῆς in ⟦James 5:5|James 5:5⟧ is the destructive judgment of God, but it is possible that σφαγῆς should be interpreted in a more literal sense of ‘destruction’ rather than mere condemnation.

s.dp: Religious Activities › Offering, Sacrifice
s.d: that which is offered as a sacrifice
s.c: The terms σφάγια and θυσίας semantically reinforce one another and are here combined essentially for emphasis.

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: to slaughter, either animals or persons; in contexts referring to persons, the implication is of violence and mercilessness{N:001}

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: a very high point on a scale of extent and in many contexts implying vehemence or violence

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: a very high point on a scale of extent and in many contexts implying vehemence or violence

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
s.d: to use a seal to close or to make something secure
s.g: to seal; to put a seal on; to make secure
s.c: For a discussion of some of the translational problems involved with ‘seal,’ see LN 6.54.

s.dp: Communication › Non-Verbal Communication
s.d: (derivative of {L:σφραγίς<SDBG:σφραγίς:000002>}[c] ‘mark, seal,’ {D:33.483}) to put a mark on something, primarily to indicate ownership but possibly also to mark group identity

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Give
s.d: to arrange to give something to someone in a secure manner
s.g: to turn over to in a secure way; to give in a secure manner
s.c: For a somewhat different interpretation of σφραγίζω in ⟦Romans 15:28|Romans 15:28⟧, see LN 15.189.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Carry, Bear
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:σφραγίζω<SDBG:σφραγίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to seal,’ {D:6.55}) to deliver something safely to a destination
s.g: to take safely to; to deliver safely
s.c: It is also possible that σφραγισάμενος in ⟦Romans 15:28|Romans 15:28⟧ serves to confirm the significance of the collection which has been raised. For a somewhat different interpretation of σφραγίζω in ⟦Romans 15:28|Romans 15:28⟧, see LN 57.87.

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: (derivative of {L:σφραγίς<SDBG:σφραγίς:000004>}[e] ‘validation,’ {D:73.9}) to demonstrate by authentic proof the truth or validity of something
s.g: to make known; to confirm; to show clearly

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
s.d: an engraved object used to make a mark denoting ownership, approval, or closure of something (normally done by pressing into heated wax and usually attached to a document or letter)
s.c: In some languages the closest equivalent to ‘seal’ or ‘signet’ is the mark made by the seal, for example, ‘the symbol of his name’ or ‘the mark of his ownership.’ In certain contexts one may employ a phrase such as ‘the instrument by which a mark is made.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
s.d: the substance which bears the imprint of a seal or signet (see {L:σφραγίς<SDBG:σφραγίς:000000>}[a], {D:6.54}), used for sealing a document or for showing ownership or endorsement
s.c: In ⟦Revelation 5:2|Revelation 5:2⟧ one may speak of ‘the wax that keeps the scroll closed,’ but in some languages it may be better to use a more general statement, for example, ‘the substance with which the scroll is sealed’ or ‘the substance that kept the scroll closed.’

s.dp: Communication › Non-Verbal Communication
s.d: the impression of a signet ring or seal, primarily indicating ownership
s.c: One may also translate this clause in ⟦Revelation 9:4|Revelation 9:4⟧ as ‘who do not have the mark on their foreheads which shows that they belong to God.’

s.dp: Communication › Written Language
s.d: the mark or impression made by a seal or stamp

s.dp: Genuine, Phony
s.d: that which confirms or attests to the genuineness of something
s.g: certification; validation; proof; evidence of genuineness

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: the joint connecting the foot to the leg

s.dp: Degree › About, Approximately, Almost, Hardly [Approximate Degree]
s.d: a degree which falls just short of some point on a scale of extent
s.c: The equivalent of this expression in ⟦Acts 13:44|Acts 13:44⟧ in some languages is ‘all the people in the town came, but some did not’ or ‘only a few of the people in town didn’t come.’

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Nature, Character
s.d: the form or nature of something, with special reference to its outer form or structure
s.c: In ⟦1 Corinthians 7:31|1 Corinthians 7:31⟧ σχῆμα does not refer to the physical form of the earth but to the way of life in the world. The reference is primarily to culture rather than to physical form. It is possible, therefore, to render this expression in ⟦1 Corinthians 7:31|1 Corinthians 7:31⟧ as ‘the way of life in this world is passing away.’

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Appearance as an Outward Manifestation of Form
s.d: appearance as an element of outward form

s.dp: Physical Impact › Split, Tear
s.d: to split or to tear an object into at least two parts
s.c: In some languages the meaning of σχίζω in ⟦Mark 1:10|Mark 1:10⟧ may be best expressed as ‘the sky tore’ or ‘there was a slit in the sky’ or possibly ‘there was suddenly an opening in the sky.’ The adverb ‘suddenly’ may provide some of the implications of the splitting involved in the verb σχίζω.

s.dp: Whole, Unite, Part, Divide › Divide
s.d: to split or divide into two parts
s.g: to divide; to split; to tear in two

s.dp: Physical Impact › Split, Tear
s.d: (derivative of {L:σχίζω<SDBG:σχίζω:000000>}[a] ‘to split, to tear,’ {D:19.27}) the condition resulting from the splitting or tearing
s.c: The separation indicated by σχίσμα may be quite different in some languages, depending upon the substance involved, for example, cloth, leather, paper, and clouds.

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Division
s.d: a division into opposing groups, generally two
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘causing division’ is literally ‘to cause two groups in place of one group,’ but more frequently the equivalent is expressed in terms of attitudes, for example, ‘to cause people to be angry at one another’ or ‘to cause people not to like one another’ or ‘to cause people to think of one another as enemies.’

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Binding and Fastening
s.d: thick cord formed by twisting or braiding several strands together; made of a variety of materials, including palm fibers, linen, or reeds
s.c: The ropes mentioned in ⟦Acts 27:32|Acts 27:32⟧ would obviously have been rather thick, while in ⟦John 2:15|John 2:15⟧ the whip which Jesus made in driving the animals and merchants out of the Temple would probably have consisted of strong cords.

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: to engage actively and earnestly in some activity over a period of time
s.g: to give time to; to devote oneself to

s.dp: Quantity › Full, Empty
s.d: to be empty, with special reference to a dwelling
s.g: to be empty; to be vacant

s.dp: Constructions › Buildings
s.d: a building where teachers and students met for study and discussion
s.c: In ⟦Acts 19:9|Acts 19:9⟧ it is better to use a translation such as ‘lecture hall’ rather than ‘school,’ since one does not wish to give the impression of the typical classroom situation characteristic of present-day schools. One may translate the relevant context of ⟦Acts 19:9|Acts 19:9⟧ as ‘every day Paul discussed with people in the lecture hall which belonged to Tyrannus’ or ‘… in a hall where Tyrannus often taught’ or ‘… lectured.’

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Cause To Be Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: to rescue from danger and to restore to a former state of safety and well being{N:001}
s.g: to deliver; to rescue; to make safe; deliverance

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Save in a Religious Sense
s.d: to cause someone to experience divine salvation

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Health, Vigor, Strength
s.d: to cause someone to become well again after having been sick{N:002}
s.g: to heal; to cure; to make well; healing
s.c: In a number of languages there are different terms for ‘healing’ depending upon the type of sickness or illness which is involved.

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Body
s.d: the physical body of persons, animals, or plants,{N:001} either dead or alive
s.c: In a number of languages a clear distinction must be made between the body of a living person and a dead body (or corpse). Other languages distinguish between the bodies of persons and the bodies of animals, and frequently the term for a body of a plant is distinct from those referring to persons or animals. Often a term for body consists of a phrase, for example, ‘flesh and bones,’ and in a number of languages a reference to the body is made primarily by referring to the person himself. For example, in ⟦Matthew 26:12|Matthew 26:12⟧ (‘has poured this ointment on my body’) the appropriate equivalent may be ‘has poured this ointment on me.’ In certain instances ‘body’ may be rendered as something which is experienced. For example, in ⟦1 Corinthians 6:20|1 Corinthians 6:20⟧ ‘glorify God through your body’ may be rendered as ‘glorify God through what you do’ or ‘… do in your body.’

s.dp: People › Human Beings
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of σῶμα[a] ‘body,’ {D:8.1}) a person as a physical being, including natural desires{N:002}

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of σῶμα[a] ‘body,’ {D:8.1}) believers in Christ who are joined together as a group, with the implication of each having a distinctive function within the group
s.c: Though in some languages it may seem relatively strange to speak of an organization of persons as a ‘body,’ it is important to try to preserve in one way or another this figurative meaning of σῶμα, since it plays such an important role in various phases of Paul’s teaching. It is frequently necessary, however, to change the metaphor into a simile, as has already been suggested in the translation of ⟦Ephesians 4:12|Ephesians 4:12⟧.

s.dp: Status › Slave, Free
s.d: a slave as property to be sold, with the probable implicaton of commerce

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Archetype, Corresponding Type [Antitype]
s.d: an entity which corresponds to an archetype or foreshadowing

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Heavenly Bodies
s.d: (an idiom, literally: heavenly body, occurring in the NT only in the plural{N:003}) the luminous objects in the sky: sun, moon, and other planets and stars
s.c: See also LN 1.8.|The phrase σῶμα ἐπουράνιον is a highly generic expression which in the plural is sometimes translatable as ‘lights in the sky,’ but more often than not it may be necessary to identify the various heavenly bodies as ‘sun, moon, and stars.’ In certain contexts one may also wish to identify the planets, often spoken of as ‘wandering stars’ or ‘moving stars’ (reflecting the etymology of the English word planet, which is derived from a Greek word meaning ‘wanderer’). These are, of course, not to be confused with shooting stars and comets in the sky.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to leave home from the body) euphemistic expressions for dying

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Body
s.d: (derivative of {L:σῶμα<SDBG:σῶμα:000000>}[a] ‘body,’ {D:8.1}) pertaining to a physical body

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Body
s.d: (derivative of {L:σῶμα<SDBG:σῶμα:000000>}[a] ‘body,’ {D:8.1}) pertaining to a physical body
s.c: It is also possible to interpret σωματικῶς in ⟦Colossians 2:9|Colossians 2:9⟧ as meaning ‘in reality,’ that is to say, ‘not symbolically’ (see LN 70.7).

s.dp: Real, Unreal
s.d: pertaining to being real (in the sense of material) in contrast with being symbolic
s.c: For another interpretation of σωματικῶς in ⟦Colossians 2:9|Colossians 2:9⟧, see LN 8.2.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian in Beroea

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Shame, Disgrace, Humiliation
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to heap coals of fire on the head, but the historical background of this idiom is not known, and hence to some extent the meaning is uncertain) to treat someone in such a positive manner as to cause that person to be ashamed or embarrassed
s.g: to cause to be ashamed; to make ashamed

s.dp: Aspect › Do Intensely or Extensively
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:σωρεύω<SDBG:σωρεύω:000000>} ‘to heap up’; see {D:25.199}) to be engaged intensively and extensively in some activity
s.g: to be given over to doing; to be fully engaged in
s.c: It is possible to interpret the usage of σωρεύομαι in ⟦2 Timothy 3:6|2 Timothy 3:6⟧ as referring to a state of being ‘burdened by sins’ or ‘burdened by the guilt of sin.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a leader of a synagogue in Corinth
s.c: Many scholars consider Σωσθένης and Σωσθένης to be the same person.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Christian of Corinth
s.c: Many scholars consider Σωσθένης and Σωσθένης to be the same person.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person who sends greetings in {S:04501602100024}

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Cause To Be Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: (derivative of {L:σῴζω<SDBG:σῴζω:000000>}[a] ‘to rescue, to save,’ {D:21.18}) one who rescues or saves

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Save in a Religious Sense
s.d: (derivative of {L:σῴζω<SDBG:σῴζω:000001>}[b] ‘to save,’ {D:21.27}) one who saves

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Cause To Be Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: to rescue from danger and to restore to a former state of safety and well being{N:001}
s.g: to deliver; to rescue; to make safe; deliverance

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Save in a Religious Sense
s.d: a state of having been saved

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Save in a Religious Sense
s.d: the process of being saved
s.c: Although it is difficult and sometimes impossible to determine whether σωτηρία refers to the state of being saved (LN 21.25) or the process of being saved, in some languages it is obligatory to choose one or the other meaning.

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Save in a Religious Sense
s.d: pertaining to divine salvation

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Save in a Religious Sense
s.d: the means by which people experience divine salvation
s.g: salvation; the way of saving; the manner of saving

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Save in a Religious Sense
s.d: the message about God saving people
s.g: the message of salvation; the message about being saved

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: to be able to reason and think properly and in a sane manner
s.g: to be in one’s right mind; to be sane; to think straight; to reason correctly
s.c: The meaning of σωφρονέω is often expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to have right thoughts,’ ‘to have one’s head,’ ‘to have straight thoughts,’ or ‘to have thoughts that do not wander.’

s.dp: Understand › Capacity for Understanding
s.d: to have understanding about practical matters and thus be able to act sensibly
s.g: to have sound judgment; to be sensible; to use good sense; sound judgment

s.dp: Communication › Teach
s.d: to instruct someone to behave in a wise and becoming manner

s.dp: Understand › Capacity for Understanding
s.d: to have understanding about practical matters and thus be able to act sensibly
s.g: to have sound judgment; to be sensible; to use good sense; sound judgment
s.c: It is also possible to understand σωφρονισμός in ⟦2 Timothy 1:7|2 Timothy 1:7⟧ as moderation and sensible behavior (see LN 88.93).

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sensible Behavior, Senseless Behavior
s.d: to behave in a sensible manner, with the implication of thoughtful awareness of what is best
s.c: For another interpretation of σωφρονισμός in ⟦2 Timothy 1:7|2 Timothy 1:7⟧, see LN 32.34.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sensible Behavior, Senseless Behavior
s.d: (derivative of the stem σωφρο ‘to behave in a sensible manner,’ {D:88.93}) pertaining to being sensible and moderate in one’s behavior
s.c: In a number of languages terms such as σωφρονισμός (LN 88.93), σωφροσύνη (LN 88.93), σώφρων, and σωφρόνως may be rendered as ‘to have right thoughts about what one should do’ or ‘to let one’s mind guide one’s body.’

s.dp: Understand › Capacity for Understanding
s.d: to have understanding about practical matters and thus be able to act sensibly
s.g: to have sound judgment; to be sensible; to use good sense; sound judgment

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sensible Behavior, Senseless Behavior
s.d: to behave in a sensible manner, with the implication of thoughtful awareness of what is best

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sensible Behavior, Senseless Behavior
s.d: (derivative of the stem σωφρο ‘to behave in a sensible manner,’ {D:88.93}) pertaining to being sensible and moderate in one’s behavior
s.c: In a number of languages terms such as σωφρονισμός (LN 88.93), σωφροσύνη (LN 88.93), σώφρων, and σωφρόνως may be rendered as ‘to have right thoughts about what one should do’ or ‘to let one’s mind guide one’s body.’

s.dp: Constructions › Buildings
s.d: a place for the lodging of travellers
s.c: ταβέρνη occurs in the NT only as a part of a place name, Τριῶν Ταβερνῶν ‘Three Taverns’ (⟦Acts 28:15|Acts 28:15⟧).
